policy: Core video-hallucination interventions, with explicit task and evaluation boundaries. General video understanding methods are candidates for related work even when they include a hallucination test. Pending moves require human approval.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 3.3, 4.1 (Benchmarks), and 4.2 (Hallucination mitigation)
records.intervention: Optimizes input visual hidden-state perturbations for a contrastive negative; model weights are not trained.
records.evaluation: VideoHallucer and EventHallusion, alongside separate general-understanding tests. Not every model/benchmark combination improves.
records.rationale: Video-grounded hallucination mitigation is the explicit design target and is directly evaluated.

original_entry.title: Mitigating Video Hallucinations via Attention-Guided Representation Perturbation
original_entry.name: ARP-CD
original_entry.description: Constructs attention-suppressed visual representations as contrastive decoding negatives to reduce unsupported video responses without updating model parameters.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 3.3, 4.1 (Benchmarks and Metrics), and 4.2 (Hallucination Benchmark Evaluation)
records.intervention: Balances spatial and temporally homogenized contrastive negatives using token-level attention divergence, without parameter learning.
records.evaluation: VidHalluc, VideoHallucer, and deterministic EventHallusion subtasks; general video benchmarks are reported separately.
records.rationale: Explicitly targets spatial and temporal video hallucinations, with direct task-specific evidence.

original_entry.title: SEASON: Mitigating Temporal Hallucination in Video Large Language Models via Self-Diagnostic Contrastive Decoding
original_entry.name: SEASON
original_entry.description: Diagnoses hallucination tendencies token by token and adaptively contrasts temporal and spatial negatives without additional training.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 5.1-5.3 (Tables 5-6)
records.intervention: LoRA supervised reasoning fine-tuning followed by thinking-based DPO that upweights human-corrected hallucinated reasoning segments.
records.evaluation: HAVEN hallucination accuracy and consistency/bias scores. Training includes replicated-image videos, but evaluation uses video questions.
records.rationale: A dedicated video-hallucination mitigation contribution; TDPO means thinking-based, not temporal, DPO.

original_entry.title: Exploring Hallucination of Large Multimodal Models in Video Understanding: Benchmark, Analysis and Mitigation
original_entry.name: Video-thinking (TDPO)
original_entry.description: Combines supervised reasoning fine-tuning with thinking-based direct preference optimization, giving fabricated reasoning stronger feedback to improve factual grounding.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 3.3 and 4.1
records.intervention: Selects sampled responses using Temporal Attention Collapse scores and stops weaker candidates at Visual Attention Vanishing, without training.
records.evaluation: Vript-HAL captions and EventHallusion QA; Video-MME and Video-MMMU are separate capability-preservation tests.
records.rationale: Explicitly minimizes video-response hallucinations through generation-time response selection.

original_entry.title: SmartSight: Mitigating Hallucination in Video-LLMs Without Compromising Video Understanding via Temporal Attention Collapse
original_entry.name: SmartSight
original_entry.description: Selects among sampled responses using temporal attention collapse and terminates unreliable generations when visual attention vanishes.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Section 4.2 (Reward Design); Section 5.1; Appendix B.2
records.intervention: SFT and reinforcement learning jointly optimize temporal grounding, answer accuracy, format, and iterative clip refinement.
records.evaluation: Long-video QA, temporal-grounding IoU, and grounded QA on VideoTemp-Bench, NextGQA, ReXTime, Charades-STA, and related general benchmarks.
records.rationale: Hallucination motivates better visual evidence, but the core contribution and reported protocol target general grounding/QA rather than dedicated video-hallucination mitigation.

original_entry.title: VideoTemp-o3: Harmonizing Temporal Grounding and Video Understanding in Agentic Thinking-with-Videos
original_entry.name: VideoTemp-o3
original_entry.description: Jointly trains temporal localization and video answering so an agent can inspect relevant clips and revise inaccurate grounding.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 3.4 and 4.1; Appendix C.1
records.intervention: Trains with textual and visual DPO preferences constructed from same-scene counterfactual action videos.
records.evaluation: VideoHallucer, EventHallusion, and VidHalluc's temporal-sequence subset, alongside CounterVid and broader tests. Synthetic-video generation is a training-data tool.
records.rationale: Directly targets unsupported action and order claims, rather than the quality of generated videos themselves.

original_entry.title: CounterVid: Counterfactual Video Generation for Mitigating Action and Temporal Hallucinations in Video-Language Models
original_entry.name: MixDPO
original_entry.description: Creates counterfactual action videos and jointly optimizes visual and textual preferences to reduce action and temporal-order hallucinations.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Section 4; Section 5.2; Appendix H.4
records.intervention: Reconstructs and aligns skeletons, parses candidate instructions into measurement queries, and injects quantitative kinematic evidence at inference.
records.evaluation: MotionHalluc directional, attributional, and temporal accuracy; reconstructed and ground-truth motion are compared separately, within Fit3D rather than unconstrained settings.
records.rationale: Explicitly reduces unsupported cross-video motion judgments; pretrained reconstruction components do not make the intervention newly trained.

original_entry.title: MotionHalluc: Diagnosing Kinematic Hallucinations in Fine-Grained Motion Reasoning
original_entry.name: PPV
original_entry.description: Injects measured physical-motion evidence into video reasoning to check kinematic claims, without training or modifying the underlying video model.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Section 3.3; Sections 4.1-4.2
records.intervention: Decomposes event queries, retrieves timestamp evidence with fixed CLIP/BLIP2, and prompts GPT-3.5 to correct video-model responses.
records.evaluation: Charades-STA-derived timestamp R@1/R@5 and event-order Yes/No accuracy. This operationalizes temporal errors, not free-form object hallucination rates.
records.rationale: Temporal-hallucination correction is the explicit central contribution; retain with the narrower event-time/order definition and metric caveat.

original_entry.title: Temporal Insight Enhancement: Mitigating Temporal Hallucination in Multimodal Large Language Models
original_entry.name: Temporal Insight
original_entry.description: Decomposes event queries into characteristic actions and uses visual-language models to estimate timestamps for temporally grounded responses.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Section 4.3; Section 5.2 (Table 4)
records.intervention: Reweights video visual features with fixed DINOv2 spatial saliency maps during inference.
records.evaluation: VidHalluc action, temporal-sequence, and scene-transition tasks with baseline/intervention comparisons; some individual scores do not improve.
records.rationale: A dedicated inference-time hallucination intervention with direct video evaluation.

original_entry.title: VidHalluc: Evaluating Temporal Hallucinations in Multimodal Large Language Models for Video Understanding
original_entry.name: DINO-HEAL
original_entry.description: Uses DINOv2 saliency to reweight visual features during inference, emphasizing informative regions without additional training of the video model.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 4.1-4.2
records.intervention: Trains a temporal-variation classifier and computes activation offsets to select and intervene in hallucination-sensitive modules.
records.evaluation: VidHalluc action/order/scene scores and EventHallusion binary accuracy.
records.rationale: Direct video-hallucination mitigation. No LLM fine-tuning does not mean training-free: the auxiliary classifier is learned.

original_entry.title: Mitigating Hallucination in VideoLLMs via Temporal-Aware Activation Engineering
original_entry.name: TAAE
original_entry.description: Uses temporal variation to identify and intervene in hallucination-sensitive model activations without further fine-tuning the language model.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Section 3.1; Section 4.1
records.intervention: Trains a multi-tool video reasoning policy with TAGPO, with optional SFT cold start and multi-granularity retrieval.
records.evaluation: MVBench, Video-MME, and LongVideoBench QA plus tool-call efficiency, not a dedicated hallucination protocol.
records.rationale: Hallucination is a motivation, but the core method and evidence address efficient long-video QA and tool use.

original_entry.title: VideoTIR: Accurate Understanding for Long Videos with Efficient Tool-Integrated Reasoning
original_entry.name: VideoTIR
original_entry.description: Uses reinforcement learning to coordinate retrieval of video clips, images, and regions for efficient, evidence-grounded long-video answers.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Section 4.2; Section 5.1
records.intervention: Learns a frame-repeat scoring module from Add-One-In correct-answer log-probability gains, then repeats selected frames.
records.evaluation: VideoMME, MLVU, LongVideoBench, LVBench, and Video-Holmes reasoning/QA accuracy.
records.rationale: Targets visual forgetting and reasoning performance; reported general QA gains do not establish dedicated hallucination mitigation. The learned scorer is not training-free.

original_entry.title: When Thinking Hurts: Mitigating Visual Forgetting in Video Reasoning via Frame Repetition
original_entry.name: FrameRepeat
original_entry.description: Trains a lightweight scoring module to repeat useful frames during reasoning and counter drift away from visual evidence.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Section 3.4; Section 4.3
records.intervention: Uses two-stage reinforcement learning for on-demand grounding and video QA, with grounding and pseudo-rewards.
records.evaluation: Multiple-choice Video-MME, LongVideoBench, and MLVU accuracy, with grounding quality/efficiency ablations.
records.rationale: A general long-video reasoning and grounding method; hallucination language is not accompanied by a dedicated reduction test in the inspected protocol.

original_entry.title: Think with Grounding: Curriculum Reinforced Reasoning with Video Grounding for Long Video Understanding
original_entry.name: Video-TwG
original_entry.description: Trains long-video models to interleave reasoning with on-demand temporal grounding through a staged reinforcement-learning curriculum.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Section II-C; Section IV-A; Section IV-D (Quantifying the CoE Advantage)
records.intervention: Jointly trains evidence grounding and concise reasoning, with evidence-alignment and answer-accuracy rewards.
records.evaluation: Includes genuine VidHal and EventHallusion evaluation alongside Video-MME, MVBench, and VSI-Bench.
records.rationale: A conservative strict-scope exclusion: the primary contribution co-optimizes general perceptual grounding and reasoning efficiency. Its explicit hallucination reward and tests remain relevant, so exclusion is not a claim that such evidence is absent.

original_entry.title: Video Evidence to Reasoning Efficient Video Understanding via Explicit Evidence Grounding
original_entry.name: CoE
original_entry.description: Extracts compact, question-relevant visual evidence and uses reinforcement learning to anchor reasoning to the selected temporal evidence.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Section 3.2; Section 4.1.1
records.intervention: Rebalances decoder visual-attention logits toward under-attended frames in selected middle-to-late layers, without training or extra decoding branches.
records.evaluation: EventHallusion and VideoHallucer. LLaVA uses paired accuracy; Qwen uses hallucinated-question accuracy, so those protocol values are not interchangeable.
records.rationale: Anchor-frame-driven hallucination is the central target, tested with dedicated video-hallucination tasks.

original_entry.title: Relaxing Anchor-Frame Dominance for Mitigating Hallucinations in Video Large Language Models
original_entry.name: DTR
original_entry.description: Rebalances decoder attention toward under-attended frames without training, changing visual encoding, or introducing auxiliary models.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Section 2; Section 3.4 (Model training); Section 4.1
records.intervention: SFT and stage-decoupled reinforcement learning train intuition, evidence retrieval, verification, and arbitration.
records.evaluation: VideoMME, LongVideoBench, MLVU answer accuracy and correction behavior, plus Haystack-LVBench retrieval metrics.
records.rationale: Targets general long-video answer correction; the inspected evidence uses correctness and rectification, not a dedicated unsupported-claim/hallucination protocol. The paper's hallucination-loop claim is not itself a measured hallucination rate.

original_entry.title: Reflect-R1: Evidence-Driven Reflection for Self-Correction in Long Video Understanding
original_entry.name: Reflect-R1
original_entry.description: Retrieves visual evidence to verify and arbitrate long-video answers, with separate reinforcement-learning objectives for each reflection stage.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Method: Overview of VTG-LLM; Experiments: Experiment Settings
records.intervention: Trains timestamp-aware embeddings, absolute-time tokens, and slot-based compression for temporal grounding.
records.evaluation: YouCook2 CIDEr/SODA/F1, Charades-STA temporal IoU recall, and QVHighlights mAP/HIT@1.
records.rationale: A temporal-grounding model, not a method whose central objective is video-hallucination mitigation. Timestamp localization accuracy alone is insufficient.

original_entry.title: VTG-LLM: Integrating Timestamp Knowledge into Video LLMs for Enhanced Video Temporal Grounding
original_entry.name: VTG-LLM
original_entry.description: Improves event timestamp localization by adding explicit time information to video tokens and using slot-based visual compression.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Section 4.1; Section 5.1 (Hallucination Evaluation Metrics; Evaluation)
records.intervention: Trains dense video-script captioning with aligned multi-scene captions, voice-over transcripts, and timestamps.
records.evaluation: Genuine Vript-HAL object/action precision, recall, and F1, alongside captioning and long-video tasks.
records.rationale: Vriptor is a general detailed-captioning model rather than a dedicated hallucination intervention. The separately introduced Vript-HAL benchmark remains eligible and must not be removed with the model.

original_entry.title: Vript: A Video Is Worth Thousands of Words
original_entry.name: Vriptor
original_entry.description: Trains a video captioning model on densely annotated videos to generate detailed descriptions of visual content and unfolding events.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 4.3, 5.1, and 5.2
records.intervention: Uses MoPE-extracted action, order, and direction matches as a composite GRPO reward following supervised fine-tuning.
records.evaluation: KPM-HA GPT-Hall and Mo-Hall, separated from generic caption metrics and QA accuracy.
records.rationale: Retain the targeted motion-hallucination post-training contribution, named GRPO with MoPE as in Section 4.3. MoPE alone is a parsing/evaluation algorithm, not the trained mitigation policy.

original_entry.title: KPM-Bench: A Kinematic Parsing Motion Benchmark for Fine-grained Motion-centric Video Understanding
original_entry.name: MoPE
original_entry.description: Uses kinematic parsing of motion descriptions as a reinforcement-learning reward to improve fine-grained video captioning and reduce motion hallucinations.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 3.4 and 4.1; Section 8 Discussion
records.intervention: Changes visual-text relative-position attention and trains a sequential visual projector while freezing vision/language backbones.
records.evaluation: General VideoQA accuracy and GPT-assisted generation quality/consistency, with qualitative hallucination cases; no dedicated hallucination-rate benchmark in the inspected evaluation.
records.rationale: The design explicitly targets hallucinated video descriptions, so retain as early direct-focus work with an evidence-strength caveat. Do not present general QA scores as a measured hallucination reduction.

original_entry.title: Vista-LLaMA: Reducing Hallucination in Video Language Models via Equal Distance to Visual Tokens
original_entry.name: Vista-LLaMA
original_entry.description: Changes visual-text attention and sequential frame projection to preserve the influence of video evidence during open-ended answer generation.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Section 4.2; Sections 5.2 and 5.5
records.intervention: Learns a Factual-Aware Evaluator and uses segment-level anti-hallucination plus answer-evidence consistency rewards for video reasoning post-training.
records.evaluation: Section 5.2 evaluates the FAE detector on VideoHallucer, reformatted HAVEN, and VidHalluc MCQ; downstream policy evaluation and reward analysis are distinct.
records.rationale: Unsupported perceptual evidence is directly penalized in the central training design. Detector accuracy is not a downstream generation hallucination rate.

original_entry.title: Decoupling Perception from Reasoning for Hallucination-Resistant Video Understanding
original_entry.name: Video-DPL
original_entry.description: Separates timestamped perceptual evidence from reasoning and uses factuality-aware process rewards to train hallucination-resistant video models.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Section 5 overview; Sections 6.1 and 6.2
records.intervention: Builds object trajectories through prompted state extraction and aggregation, then retrieves trajectories to answer each query without parameter updates.
records.evaluation: STRAND unconditional joint Faithful Accuracy and VideoHallucer, separated from general Video-MME and EgoSchema accuracy.
records.rationale: Directly targets hallucinated object states, relations, and temporal reasoning. Conditional consistency alone is not the primary faithfulness measure.

original_entry.title: STRAND: Benchmarking and Improving Object-Centric Spatio-Temporal Monitoring in Video Large Language Models
original_entry.name: STRAND (Trajectory Reasoning)
original_entry.description: Combines structured visual trajectories with symbolic aggregation to answer object-centric spatiotemporal questions using a fixed video-language model.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Strategies for Mitigating SAH (position encoding and DPO)
records.intervention: DPO trains caption preferences using within-video or out-of-video hallucinated negatives.
records.evaluation: ELV-Halluc average accuracy and SAH ratio, with Video-MME as a separate general-capability check.
records.rationale: Direct long-video semantic-aggregation mitigation. The best SAH reduction uses 4k in-video pairs, not the combined 8k setting; SAH ratio and overall hallucination are distinct.

original_entry.title: ELV-Halluc: Benchmarking Semantic Aggregation Hallucinations in Long Video Understanding
original_entry.name: ELV-Halluc-DPO
original_entry.description: Trains on adversarial preference pairs to reduce long-video hallucinations caused by incorrectly combining semantic information across video segments.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 4.2, 5.2, and 5.3
records.intervention: Trains offline-to-online video understanding with a pyramid memory bank and interleaved streaming instruction data.
records.evaluation: OVBench and generic offline VideoQA accuracy; OVBench includes temporal-hallucination subtasks within a broader streaming suite.
records.rationale: Core contribution is general streaming perception, memory, and reasoning rather than a dedicated video-hallucination intervention.

original_entry.title: Online Video Understanding: OVBench and VideoChat-Online
original_entry.name: VideoChat-Online
original_entry.description: Combines pyramid memory with offline-to-online instruction training to support streaming-video perception, memory, and reasoning over continuously arriving frames.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Section 3.4; Section 4.1 (benchmarks, metrics, implementation)
records.intervention: Learns tracklet-phrase contrastive alignment using self-generated hallucinative negatives and an action-squeezer.
records.evaluation: FactVC and weighted-HalFscore on video captions plus VidHal QA; Dream1k description quality is separate.
records.rationale: Joint object/action hallucination mitigation is the central method objective, with explicit caption-level faithfulness evaluation.

original_entry.title: Mitigating Object and Action Hallucinations in Multimodal LLMs via Self-Augmented Contrastive Alignment
original_entry.name: SANTA
original_entry.description: Combines hallucination-based negative captions with tracklet-phrase contrastive alignment to improve object and action faithfulness in video descriptions.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Temporal Contrastive Decoding; TCD Evaluation (implementation and effectiveness)
records.intervention: Contrasts original-video logits with temporally downsampled-video logits during decoding.
records.evaluation: EventHallusion binary accuracy on three video-language backbones.
records.rationale: Explicit event-hallucination mitigation without training; improvements are benchmark-specific and not universal per-subset gains.

original_entry.title: EventHallusion: Diagnosing Event Hallucinations in Video LLMs
original_entry.name: TCD
original_entry.description: Contrasts predictions from original and temporally disrupted video sequences during decoding to reduce event hallucinations without additional model training.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 3.3 and 4.1
records.intervention: Adds tracked object-ID visual prompts and learns grounding through temporal IoU, spatial consistency, and format rewards.
records.evaluation: HCSTVG, ST-Align, Charades-STA, TVGBench and MeViS localization/segmentation metrics.
records.rationale: Addresses coordinate/timestamp prediction errors in grounding, not unsupported video-language claims under the catalog's strict hallucination scope. IoU and mask accuracy are not hallucination rates.

original_entry.title: STVG-R1: Incentivizing Instance-Level Reasoning and Grounding in Videos via Reinforcement Learning
original_entry.name: STVG-R1
original_entry.description: Replaces coordinate prediction with visually prompted object identities and reinforcement learning for spatially and temporally consistent video grounding.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections III-C, IV-A, IV-C1/2, and IV-D2
records.intervention: Uses fixed detectors and captioners for object-grounded rectification and prominence-guided iterative caption refinement.
records.evaluation: MSVD/MSR-VTT object-coverage metrics and a human study rating unsupported/incorrect caption content.
records.rationale: Retain the explicit post-hoc visual-faithfulness intervention with a metric caveat: its automatic Temporal Inconsistency measures omitted salient objects, not fabricated objects. The reported human inconsistency improvement is a rating change, not a hallucination incidence rate.

original_entry.title: ProCap: Prominence-guided Object Rectification for Faithful and Comprehensive Video Captioning
original_entry.name: ProCap
original_entry.description: Ranks detected objects by prominence and iteratively revises captions to reduce omissions and hallucinations without retraining the captioning model.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 4.3, 5.1, and 5.4
records.intervention: Scales DPO margins and loss weights with action-error severity to penalize incorrect or fabricated limb-motion claims.
records.evaluation: FlexBench GPA and Weighted Hallucination Rate, with caption length/shot structure and generic QA reported separately.
records.rationale: Direct motion-hallucination alignment; reported WHR reduction varies by backbone and is distinct from aggregate GPA gain.

original_entry.title: Beyond Binary Preferences: Graded Preference Optimization for Limb-Motion Captioning
original_entry.name: GM-DPO
original_entry.description: Weights direct preference optimization by the severity of fabricated or incorrect limb actions, promoting physically faithful, person-specific video captions.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Section 3.3; Section 4.2; Section 5.1 instruction tuning
records.intervention: Trains with disentangled spatial-temporal attention and Harmonic-RoPE to suppress spurious action-scene associations.
records.evaluation: UNSCENE dual-question correctness and open-ended action/scene scoring; generic VideoQA metrics are separate.
records.rationale: Action-scene hallucination is the explicit design target and receives dedicated evaluation.

original_entry.title: MASH-VLM: Mitigating Action-Scene Hallucination in Video-LLMs through Disentangled Spatial-Temporal Representations
original_entry.name: MASH-VLM
original_entry.description: Disentangles spatial and temporal attention and introduces Harmonic RoPE to reduce confusion between depicted actions and surrounding scene context.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Section 5 prompt-aware MIL formulation; Section 6.1 implementation and benchmarks
records.intervention: Updates the model with prompt-aware multi-instance video preference optimization using augmented rejected clips.
records.evaluation: Official VideoHallucer and EventHallusion protocols, plus separate general video benchmarks.
records.rationale: Direct video-response hallucination mitigation. No additional parameters or preference annotation does not mean training-free.

original_entry.title: PaMi-VDPO: Mitigating Video Hallucinations by Prompt-Aware Multi-Instance Video Preference Learning
original_entry.name: PaMi-VDPO
original_entry.description: Learns video preferences online using prompt-aware augmented clips as rejected inputs, reducing incorrect rejections during hallucination mitigation training.

records.inspected_sections: Official IJCAI PDF: Abstract, Introduction, Sections 3.1-3.4 and 4.1-4.3 (pp. 9167-9172)
records.intervention: Trains Q-Former and a text encoder with multilevel semantic-discriminative alignment and two-stage task learning; the vision encoder and LLM remain frozen.
records.evaluation: LVU content/metadata top-1 accuracy and MSVD VideoQA accuracy, plus qualitative examples; no dedicated hallucination-rate protocol in the inspected experiments.
records.rationale: Retain for its explicit central hallucination-mitigation objective, but mark indirect evaluation evidence. General classification/QA improvements do not quantify hallucination reduction.

original_entry.title: Hallucination Reduction in Video-Language Models via Hierarchical Multimodal Consistency
original_entry.name: MMA
original_entry.description: Combines multi-level semantic alignment with progressive training to reduce hallucinations caused by weak discrimination between video and language concepts.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 4.4, 5.1, and 5.2 open-ended generation
records.intervention: Trains clue extraction, differentiable clue gating, and clue-conditioned reasoning with supervised losses.
records.evaluation: NExT-QA, STAR, MVBench accuracy and NExT-OE WUPS semantic similarity.
records.rationale: General clue-guided VideoQA is the core evaluated task. WUPS and answer accuracy do not establish a measured unsupported-claim reduction despite the paper's hallucination wording.

original_entry.title: Clue Matters: Leveraging Latent Visual Clues to Empower Video Reasoning
original_entry.name: ClueNet
original_entry.description: Separately supervises visual clue extraction and answer reasoning, then filters clues for faithful and interpretable video question answering.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 3.3 and 4.1
records.intervention: GRPO trains event-graph-guided reasoning with visual-attention, accuracy, and format rewards.
records.evaluation: Official VidHalluc ACH/TSH accuracy and STH score; RexTime grounding and QA are separate.
records.rationale: Directly targets weak visual grounding and temporal reasoning hallucinations, with dedicated video-hallucination evaluation.

original_entry.title: GraphThinker: Reinforcing Temporally Grounded Video Reasoning with Event Graph Thinking
original_entry.name: GraphThinker
original_entry.description: Builds event-based video scene graphs and applies visual-attention rewards during reinforcement fine-tuning to ground temporal reasoning.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Section 4.2; Section 5.1 benchmarks; Section 5.4
records.intervention: Optimizes input object/frame masks using query-side gradients, then applies contrastive decoding while model parameters stay fixed.
records.evaluation: EventHallusion and a video-adapted POPE absent-object test; general QA benchmarks are separate.
records.rationale: Dedicated hallucination intervention. Input-mask optimization does not constitute model training; the video-POPE test is a custom subset protocol.

original_entry.title: MACD: Model-Aware Contrastive Decoding via Counterfactual Data
original_entry.name: MACD
original_entry.description: Uses model feedback to construct object-level counterfactual video inputs for evidence-grounded contrastive decoding.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Section 4.3; Section 5.1 evaluations
records.intervention: Trains a residual MLP aligner for spatiotemporal and semantic consistency with a frozen backbone.
records.evaluation: VideoHallucer, EventHallusion, and VideoHallu; ActivityNet-QA and MMVU assess general ability.
records.rationale: Explicit video-hallucination mitigation. Inference-time insertion and a frozen backbone do not make the learned aligner training-free.

original_entry.title: Enhancing Video Representations with Spatiotemporal-Semantic Residual to Mitigate Hallucinations in Video Large Multimodal Models
original_entry.name: ViSSRes
original_entry.description: Trains a lightweight residual aligner on frozen video representations to improve spatiotemporal consistency and alignment with response semantics.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Section III-C reasoning-demand reward; Section IV-B benchmarks and Table II
records.intervention: SFT and GRPO teach tree-guided cue localization with rewards scaled by question reasoning demand.
records.evaluation: Six general reasoning/understanding benchmarks and genuine VideoHallucer evaluation; the latter improves average accuracy but not every category.
records.rationale: Strict-scope boundary recommendation: the central contribution is general perception-aware video reasoning, with hallucination evaluation as an additional benefit. This is not a claim that hallucination evidence is absent.

original_entry.title: Video-ToC: Video Tree-of-Cue Reasoning
original_entry.name: Video-ToC
original_entry.description: Localizes visual evidence through a tree of cues and trains reasoning with rewards adjusted to the video's reasoning demands.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 4.3 and 4.4 contrastive-decoding results
records.intervention: Contrasts logits with a scene-matched, semantically exclusive counterfactual counterpart supplied by CCTVBench.
records.evaluation: CCTVBench instance classification and strict quadruple consistency, with negative hallucination diagnostics.
records.rationale: Targets unsupported traffic-event assertions, but depends on paired counterfactual videos at inference; do not imply an unrestricted single-video deployment method.

original_entry.title: CCTVBench: Contrastive Consistency Traffic VideoQA Benchmark for Multimodal LLMs
original_entry.name: C-TCD
original_entry.description: Uses counterfactual traffic-video counterparts during contrastive decoding to improve the consistency of accident-related judgments without additional model training.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 3.4 and 4.1
records.intervention: Combines input-conditioned attention reallocation and per-frame evidence erasure with contrastive decoding; all model parameters remain frozen.
records.evaluation: VidHalluc, VideoHallucer, EventHallusion, with general video benchmarks reported separately.
records.rationale: Direct video-hallucination mitigation. Training-free does not mean hyperparameter-free; the source reports source-setting calibration.

original_entry.title: VADER: Adaptive Debiasing for Hallucination Mitigation in Video Large Language Models
original_entry.name: VADER
original_entry.description: Adaptively reweights visual attention and contrasts selectively erased evidence to suppress prior-driven video hallucinations without training.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 3.3, 5.3, 6, and 8
records.intervention: Blindly re-captions cited video frames and uses an off-the-shelf pretrained NLI classifier to tag drafted claims as Grounded or Unverified.
records.evaluation: Forty claims from 12 questions on one animated video, including adversarial false premises; no broad held-out benchmark or confidence intervals.
records.rationale: Direct post-hoc video-claim verification, not answer rewriting. Catch rate measures verification on a small controlled sample, not generation improvement or broad generalization. No task-specific NLI training is introduced.

original_entry.title: Catching Hallucinated Citations in Video-LLM Question Answering: A Self-Verification Pipeline and Verifier Ablation Study
original_entry.name: GroundedVQA
original_entry.description: Verifies timestamped video-answer claims by independently re-captioning cited frames and checking textual entailment with a separate model.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 3.3, 4.1, and 4.5
records.intervention: Trains HGB and target-pilot logistic reliability scorers over fixed model/view responses; does not change any generated answer.
records.evaluation: Held-out HERBench and Perception Test AURC, AUROC, calibration and selective risk; VHD is used for development and diagnosis.
records.rationale: Recommend moving out of the core mitigation list into related reliability work. The method targets general answer-risk ranking under shift, not answer correction or video-specific claim verification. Retain the separate VHD benchmark; lower selective risk is not lower full-coverage hallucination incidence.

original_entry.title: Target-Checked Reliability Score Refinement for Video Question Answering
original_entry.name: TRACE-RC
original_entry.description: Refines learned reliability scores through target-checked evidence across video samplings, improving answer selection while leaving generated answers unchanged.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 5.2 and 6.1
records.intervention: Trains instance-, temporal-, and perceptive-level DPO with spatially and temporally grounded preferences.
records.evaluation: VideoHallucer and EventHallusion; general QA and caption quality are separate.
records.rationale: Directly targets video-language misalignment and hallucinated responses with dedicated evaluation.

original_entry.title: VistaDPO: Video Hierarchical Spatial-Temporal Direct Preference Optimization for Large Video Models
original_entry.name: VistaDPO
original_entry.description: Optimizes preferences at whole-video, temporal, and object levels using spatially and temporally annotated response pairs.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Section 3.2 Method Overview, experimental setup, and Tables 2-3
records.intervention: Reported GRPO post-training mixes counterintuitive synthetic-video QA and real-video QA, with a ROUGE-based answer reward.
records.evaluation: VideoHallu counterintuitive-video answer accuracy, with MMVU and MVBench checking general performance.
records.rationale: The method explicitly counters language/physics priors overriding visible video evidence. This is a video-understanding intervention, not video-generation quality control. Implementation was not replicated: the source's Equation 2 has a pairwise DPO form despite its GRPO label, whereas the training narrative names Open-R1 and a ROUGE reward.

original_entry.title: VideoHallu: Evaluating and Mitigating Multi-modal Hallucinations on Synthetic Video Understanding
original_entry.name: VideoHallu-GRPO
original_entry.description: Applies group relative policy optimization to help video models recognize physical and logical violations instead of substituting familiar prior expectations.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 3.4 and 4.3
records.intervention: Trains perturbation-selection and saliency-fusion controllers with REINFORCE, then combines original, negative, and positive decoding branches.
records.evaluation: OmniVCHall isolated and compositional yes/no and multiple-choice accuracy.
records.rationale: Dedicated compositional video-hallucination mitigation. Frozen VLLM weights do not make the learned controllers training-free.

original_entry.title: Learning to Decode Against Compositional Hallucination in Video Multimodal Large Language Models
original_entry.name: TriCD
original_entry.description: Learns an adaptive controller for triple-path contrastive decoding, combining video perturbations and saliency enhancement to address compositional hallucinations.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 4.2 and 5.1
records.intervention: Adds sink-token penalties to existing spatial/temporal pruning rules to preserve visual information under small token budgets.
records.evaluation: Genuine EventHallusion binary/description evaluation alongside VideoComp, VCG-Bench, and generic VideoQA under 10-20% token retention.
records.rationale: Strict-scope boundary recommendation: core objective is efficient token pruning while preserving fine-grained understanding. Hallucination is a diagnostic and benefit, not the sole dedicated task; this is not an image-only method or a claim that no hallucination evaluation exists.

original_entry.title: Sink-Token-Aware Pruning for Fine-Grained Video Understanding in Efficient Video LLMs
original_entry.name: SToP
original_entry.description: Identifies attention sink tokens and suppresses them during visual token pruning to preserve fine-grained grounding and hallucination robustness.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 5.5 and 6.3
records.intervention: Trains patch scoring, query conditioning, and routed experts to disentangle misleading overlay text from native video evidence.
records.evaluation: VisualTextTrap resistance, vulnerability, answer-shift and conflict-intensity metrics under positive/negative/neutral overlays.
records.rationale: Directly targets text-overlay-induced hallucinated video claims; learned auxiliary modules mean training is required.

original_entry.title: When Text Hijacks Vision: Benchmarking and Mitigating Text Overlay-Induced Hallucination in Vision Language Models
original_entry.name: VTHM-MoE
original_entry.description: Trains specialized experts with dual encoders and adaptive token routing to disentangle misleading text overlays from underlying visual evidence.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 3.3 and 4.1
records.intervention: Selects uncertain tokens, reinjects frozen projected evidence in middle layers, and contrasts temporal counterfactuals in later decoding layers.
records.evaluation: EventHallusion and VidHalluc, with NExT-QA and MVBench general evaluation; complete cross-backbone runs are not reported for every benchmark.
records.rationale: Explicit spatiotemporal hallucination mitigation. The inspected version states reinjection tensors are constructed at inference without learned additions.

original_entry.title: STEAR: Layer-Aware Spatiotemporal Evidence Intervention for Hallucination Mitigation in Video Large Language Models
original_entry.name: STEAR
original_entry.description: Targets risky decoding steps with layer-specific visual evidence, combining grounding restoration with temporal counterfactual checks.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Section 3.3; Sections 4.1 benchmarks and 4.2 hallucination evaluation
records.intervention: Trains caption policies with structured factual scene-graph, temporal, and video-grounded VQA rewards using sequence-level REINFORCE.
records.evaluation: VideoHallucer and EventHallusion, with temporal/general QA metrics separately reported.
records.rationale: Reducing unsupported factual and temporal caption content is central, rather than an incidental consequence of generic QA optimization.

original_entry.title: Reinforcing Consistency in Video MLLMs with Structured Rewards
original_entry.name: Structured Rewards
original_entry.description: Audits captions as factual and temporal claims, then trains with scene-graph, temporal, and video-grounded self-verification rewards.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Section 3.3.4; Section 4.1 evaluation benchmarks
records.intervention: Trains a visual token patcher using answer supervision, information-guided rank calibration, and sparsity regularization with a frozen backbone.
records.evaluation: VideoHallucer, Vript-HAL, and VidHalluc; Video-MMMU and ActivityNet-QA are general-capability checks.
records.rationale: Direct hallucination mitigation through learned token repair. Ground-truth answers are used during training, not inference.

original_entry.title: MultiToP: Learning to Patch Visual Tokens to Mitigate Hallucinations in Video Large Multimodal Models
original_entry.name: MultiToP
original_entry.description: Trains a lightweight patcher to selectively replace unreliable visual tokens before generation while leaving the original video model unchanged.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Section 4.2 audio alignment and LoRA FT; Appendix F
records.intervention: Trains audio alignment and LoRA adaptations on audio-visual hallucination-aware questions.
records.evaluation: AVHBench audio-driven video and video-driven audio hallucination tasks; captioning/matching and VAST/AVinstruct are distinct outcomes.
records.rationale: Explicit cross-modal hallucination mitigation with direct audio-induced false visual-claim evaluation; not audio-only research.

original_entry.title: AVHBench: A Cross-Modal Hallucination Benchmark for Audio-Visual Large Language Models
original_entry.name: AVHModel-Align-FT
original_entry.description: Fine-tunes audio-visual models with benchmark-derived training data to improve cross-modal alignment and robustness against auditory and visual hallucinations.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 3.2, 4.1, and 4.2
records.intervention: Uses modality-dominance-aware attentive masking, trimodal contrastive logits, and entropy-gated extra decoding without parameter updates.
records.evaluation: AVHBench cross-modal hallucination evaluation; MUSIC-AVQA, MSVD-QA and ActivityNet-QA are separate general tasks.
records.rationale: Direct audio-visual hallucination intervention. Video-only QA gains alone are not proof of video-only hallucination reduction; the direct evidence comes from the audio-visual conditions.

original_entry.title: AVCD: Mitigating Hallucinations in Audio-Visual Large Language Models through Contrastive Decoding
original_entry.name: AVCD
original_entry.description: Uses modality-aware masking and confidence-guided contrastive decoding to suppress hallucinations across audio, video, and language without training.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 3.3 and 5.2; Appendix E
records.intervention: Multi-round DPO ranks captions by atomic-event hallucination/omission and repetition metrics, updating the reference and LoRA modules between rounds.
records.evaluation: Audio-visual caption missing and hallucinated event rates against annotated event lists, with total error and general QA reported separately.
records.rationale: Retain the targeted hallucination-aware preference objective, not an unrestricted endorsement of the whole captioning model. Total error combines omissions and hallucinations and must not be described as hallucination rate alone.

original_entry.title: Enhancing Multimodal LLM for Detailed and Accurate Video Captioning using Multi-Round Preference Optimization
original_entry.name: mrDPO
original_entry.description: Improves audio-visual captions through repeated preference optimization and rebirth tuning designed to retain non-captioning abilities.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 5.1-5.2 and Table 3; Appendix B.2
records.intervention: Prompts modality/emotion knowledge extraction, an initial prediction, explanation and verification, then a revised binary answer.
records.evaluation: EmotionHallucer-P mixed-modality paired QA, including video conditions; Table 3 reports pooled results rather than isolated video-only gains.
records.rationale: Dedicated multimodal emotion-hallucination intervention with a video application. Scope is limited to video/audio-visual inputs; the pooled 9.9-point improvement is not a video-only result.

original_entry.title: EmotionHallucer: Evaluating Emotion Hallucinations in Multimodal Large Language Models
original_entry.name: PEP-MEK
original_entry.description: Combines perception-enhanced prompting with memory-based emotion knowledge to reduce emotion hallucinations without additional training of the multimodal model.
